Subject: Segregation hosting economics and accelerator selection

Hi Rafael —

Thanks for taking the quick intro yesterday. We’re trying to firm up a recommendation for the execs on whether Helix should go with a Redwood Dedicated pool (reserved) or the Private deployment (VPC / on-prem) for our patient-data workloads. Key asks from our side:

- Clear capacity sizing tied to expected QPS and tokens/workload patterns
- Which accelerators you’d recommend (H100 vs A100 vs smaller L-class) for cost vs latency
- Resiliency considerations and procurement timeline implications
- Any SOC2 / evidence footprint differences (Asha will own compliance questions)

High level workload: 120 peak concurrent sessions at launch, average session ~80 tokens request/response (we push prompt + 40-50 response), p95 latency target ~150ms for inference. Burst factor could be 2.5x during mornings.

Can you sketch a comparative recommendation and next steps for procurement? We’ll loop procurement after we have a clear ask.

—Jordan
Jordan Lee | Head of Integrations, ClearPath Health
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Segregation hosting economics and accelerator selection

Jordan —

Appreciate the detail. I pulled together a short comparison and a pragmatic GPU mix recommendation keyed to your SLOs and the regulated nature of your data. Attached: redwood_private_vs_dedicated_onepager.pdf and a simple cost/throughput model (redwood_gpu_mix_model.xlsx). High-level summary below.

1) Sizing assumptions we used (feel free to correct):
   • Peak concurrent sessions: 120
   • Avg tokens per request: 80 (prompt+response)
   • Target inference P95: 150ms
   • Typical model: 13B–70B family (we left model flexible; conservative perf modeled on a 33B-like variant quantized to 8-bit)

2) Dedicated (Redwood-managed reserved pool) — recommendation for Helix pilot:
   • Baseline: 4 x A100 80GB (reserved) for steady throughput. A100 provides stable quantized 8-bit perf and lower unit cost than H100 for many decoder-only models.
   • Burst capacity: autoscale to 12 vGPU-equivalent tiles via shared burst pool (adds 2–3x on-demand capacity)
   • Upside: fast procurement (we manage infra), SOC2 evidence packaged, single-tenant logical isolation, simpler upgrades/rollouts
   • Downside: logical isolation still routes via Redwood control plane (if you need full air-gap this is not enough)

3) Private (VPC or on-prem) — recommendation if Helix requires physical separation / air-gapped operations:
   • Baseline: 6 x H100 80GB (for model headroom and lower latency at larger context / KV cache sizes). H100s excel for larger models and when multi-instance batching is heavy.
   • Redundancy: +2 hot spares recommended for maintenance windows (8 total recommended for ~5x steady headroom)
   • Upside: full control of networking/data path, suitable for strict regulators; direct KMS/HSM integrations under your tenancy
   • Downside: longer procurement (30–90 days), higher upfront opex/capex, Redwood private deploy support contract required

4) Cost vs latency tradeoffs (very high level):
   • A100 reserved fleet (Dedicated) gives you the best cost per token for steady-state quantized inference.
   • H100 private fleet gives better tail latency for larger models and headroom for future model upgrades, but at a higher per-hour cost.

5) Operational and QA notes:
   • We recommend an MLQA pass with a small eval suite (we can reuse your PII redaction tests) before switching models between fleets.
   • KV/prefix caching will reduce tokens by ~20–35% for repeated prompts; factoring that in reduces baseline fleet size notably.

Next steps I suggest:
   1) Confirm model target (13B vs 33B vs 70B) so we can finalize GPU counts in the spreadsheet.
   2) Marissa will follow up with a short Dedicated pricing milestone and a Private deployment service estimate.
   3) Asha — if you can emit the SOC2 / encryption evidence checklist items you need, we’ll map them to the deployment choices.

I’ll leave Marissa to scope the procurement ask. If helpful we can run a short 90-minute sizing call with your infra and security teams.

—Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference

Thanks Rafael — this is helpful. A couple of clarifying questions from procurement and infra: 

1) Burst behavior: in Dedicated you mention autoscale to a shared burst pool. Does that rely on cross-tenant capacity? If yes, procurement will want a guaranteed fallback if the shared pool is exhausted.
2) Encryption/KMS: for Private we plan to use our HSM and internal KMS. For Dedicated, what are the supported KMS integration patterns (bring-your-own KMS or envelope encryption)?

On the model target, we’re aiming initially for a 33B-equivalent that we’ll test; if the results are acceptable we may step to a 70B in Q4.

—Jordan

Jordan / Rafael —

Looping in Karthik (deal engineering) and Soojin (customer success). Short answers while we prep a formal pricing doc: 

1) Shared burst pool guarantees: we can add a capacity hedge SLA to the Dedicated offer — essentially a committed buffer you pay for (configurable months). If required, we can also offer a soft-fallback to a Private burst (customer-owned) during high-impact windows.

2) KMS integrations for Dedicated: we support envelope encryption with customer-managed keys (bring-your-own KMS) by integrating via AWS KMS, GCP KMS, or your own HSM via customer connector. For Private on-prem, full HSM ownership is supported. We’ll list exact integration patterns in the security doc (attached: helix_soc2_questions.pdf).

3) Pricing path suggestion:
   • Pilot (90 days): 4 A100 reserved + burst hedge (monthly) — we’ll include a 20% pilot discount for new enterprise pilots.
   • Private estimate (30–60 day lead): 6 H100 baseline + 2 spares — we’ll provide a separate capex/opex sheet.

Karthik — please prep a quick committed vs on-demand cost ladder in the spreadsheet Rafael attached and I’ll turn that into a purchase-ready quote.

—Marissa
